title: Virtue as the Foundation of the House
english: To prefer something over God. Since God is to be loved most in a time of struggle, in a time of persecution, the love of God must be preferred above all. If one pulls away from parents or the old age of a parent, 'honor God, since you are not able to follow me' (Exodus 20:12). Therefore, to hate the father and the mother does not mean that kind of hatred by which we are provoked and loathe, but rather according to not preferring them to God. In this same way, [one treats] the wife and the children, and in this same way, the brothers. 'And he will hate even his own soul' (Matthew 10:22), he says. He hates his own soul while enduring death for the sake of a witness, but on account of the Savior; for see what he says: he who hates a father 'because of me' (Matthew 10:37), not utterly. The Savior is to be preferred above all. Just as if someone hates a mother because of the Savior. This hatred does not bring slander. He who thus has hated the parents for the sake of the Savior is abandoned by them. Therefore he says: 'for my father and my mother have abandoned me' (Psalm 27:10). The abandonment is unto the end. Psalm of a song of the dedication of a house; to David.

A resurrection occurs both according to the soul and according to the body; 'Awake, sleeper, and arise from the dead, and Christ will shine upon you' (Isaiah 26:19). Here, the one sinning is dead; for 'the soul, the one sinning, this one shall die' (Ezekiel 18:4); and: 'sin, having been completed, brings death' (Romans 6:23) to the one sinning. Therefore, awaken this one into the life that was before the fall; for this was the life with virtue. Thus also in Jeremiah it is said: 'Does not he who has fallen rise again?' (Jeremiah 31:12); and a resurrection also happens to the body; for its formation was not its fall, but the corruption after the formation. Therefore also it itself rises. And in general we say this: the beautiful leads the bad. For indeed even bad craftsmanship is after the art, and the error after the correct, and the transgression after the law; for transgression is nothing other than a [deviation].

The command is given. And again, the 'para-' prefix is always used to signify deviation: 'to think wrongly', 'to overlook', 'to step aside'. Therefore, virtue is the first thing; for observe where the word flows: the rational has come to be so that it might possess virtue; for it did not come to be so that it might possess wickedness, since virtue was the very thing that was the opposite of wickedness. Since almost all begin from sin when they reach into material life, if it were granted that the soul never lived before material life, then things began from wickedness, and sin is not actually sin, but rather virtue; for no one is said to sin by doing what is natural or what is characteristic of their nature. Those who practice arts and act according to them, when they do what is characteristic of the art, are not said to think wrongly or to step aside.

Thus, it is the building up of the fallen house and the return from captivity. According to a former principle, we say that the inhabitant and the house are the same thing. But it can also be taken more universally: the sum of the faithful, the church, is the house; 'that you may know how one must conduct oneself in the house of God' (1 Timothy 3:15); and 'I have loved the beauty of your house' (Psalm 26:8). And those who inhabit it are these faithful ones, those living according to virtue. But if the soul is the house, the earnest thoughts which are connatural with it are the inhabitants. Then both the building up and the dedication happen at once. And renovation occurs when those who were previously outside of it take up habitation within it again.

'A psalm of song'. We said when we began the twentieth psalm, that they are psalms, they are songs, they are psalms of song and songs of psalms. And we were saying that the psalm signifies the practice. And the one singing strikes an instrument called a psaltery.
